facts.fact: WordStream reports that the average cost-per-click for dental keywords is $6.69.
facts.quote: the average CPC for dental keywords is $6.69

facts.fact: Adwave's page estimates that Google Ads costs $1,000 to $3,000 per month for dental practices.
facts.quote: $1,000 to $3,000/month for Google Ads

facts.fact: The page states that Google Local Services Ads charge $25 to $75 per lead.
facts.quote: LSAs charge $25 to $75 per lead

facts.fact: The page states that Google Business Profile optimization is free.
facts.quote: Google Business Profile optimization is free.

facts.fact: The page estimates that Meta (Facebook and Instagram) ads cost $500 to $2,000 per month for most single-location dental practices.
facts.quote: $500 to $2,000/month for most single-location practices

facts.fact: The page estimates that new patient acquisition through Meta typically costs $50 to $150 per booked appointment.
facts.quote: New patient acquisition costs through Meta typically run $50 to $150 per booked appointment.

facts.fact: The page advises that Meta ad creative needs a refresh every 4 to 6 weeks.
facts.quote: Requires creative refresh every 4 to 6 weeks.

facts.fact: The page gives an example of a dental new-patient special of a $99 exam, X-ray, and cleaning.
facts.quote: new patient specials ($99 exam, X-ray, and cleaning)

facts.fact: The page says CTV planning bands on its average-CPM page run about $15 to $35.
facts.quote: CTV planning bands on the average-CPM page run about $15 to $35.

facts.fact: Adwave media starts at $30 per day prepaid, which the page says is about $900 in a 30-day month.
facts.quote: Adwave media starts at **$30/day** prepaid, which is about $900 in a 30-day month.

facts.fact: The page states that a shorter-than-monthly test is possible only if the flight is shorter than a full month or the buy is outside this product, and that $200 should not be treated as an Adwave monthly floor.
facts.quote: Do not treat $200 as an Adwave monthly floor.

facts.fact: Thinkbox research, as cited by the page, finds TV advertising generates 2.2 times more trust than digital display.
facts.quote: TV advertising generates 2.2 times more trust than digital display

facts.fact: BrightLocal research, as cited by the page, finds 87% of consumers read online reviews for local businesses.
facts.quote: BrightLocal, 87% of consumers read online reviews for local businesses

facts.fact: The page estimates that review management platforms cost $100 to $300 per month.
facts.quote: Review management platforms run $100 to $300/month.

facts.fact: The page estimates that dental SEO specialists charge $1,000 to $2,500 per month.
facts.quote: Dental SEO specialists charge $1,000 to $2,500/month.

facts.fact: The page says automated review services such as Birdeye or Podium can generate 20 to 50 new reviews per month.
facts.quote: Services like Birdeye or Podium automate this process and can generate 20 to 50 new reviews per month.

facts.fact: The page states that local SEO takes 3 to 6 months to show significant results.
facts.quote: Takes 3 to 6 months to see significant results.

facts.fact: EDDM direct mailers cost $0.20 to $0.50 per piece, according to the page.
facts.quote: EDDM mailers run $0.20 to $0.50 per piece.

facts.fact: A 5,000-piece targeted direct mailing costs $1,000 to $2,500, according to the page.
facts.quote: A 5,000-piece targeted mailing costs $1,000 to $2,500.

facts.fact: Community sponsorships for dental practices range from $200 to $1,000, according to the page.
facts.quote: Community sponsorships range from $200 to $1,000.

facts.fact: The page states that direct mail response rates are 1% to 3%.
facts.quote: Lower response rates (1% to 3%).

facts.fact: A common dental referral program structure gives existing patients a credit of $25 to $50 toward their next visit for each new patient referred.
facts.quote: existing patients receive a credit ($25 to $50 toward their next visit) for each new patient they refer.

facts.fact: The page states that acquiring a new patient costs 5 to 10 times more than retaining an existing one.
facts.quote: Acquiring a new patient costs 5 to 10 times more than retaining an existing one.

facts.fact: The page states that automated appointment reminders reduce no-shows by 30% to 50%.
facts.quote: Reduces no-shows by 30% to 50%.

facts.fact: The page states that dental email marketing platforms cost $20 to $200 per month depending on platform and list size.
facts.quote: $20 to $200/month depending on platform and list size.

facts.fact: The page's channel table lists a monthly budget of $1,000-$3,000 for Google Ads / LSAs, with a patient acquisition cost of $100-$300, as a planning band.
facts.quote: | Google Ads / LSAs | $1,000-$3,000 | 1-2 weeks | $100-$300 | Active searchers |

facts.fact: The page's channel table lists a monthly budget of $500-$2,000 for Meta (Facebook/Instagram), with a patient acquisition cost of $50-$150, as a planning band.
facts.quote: | Meta (Facebook/Instagram) | $500-$2,000 | 2-4 weeks | $50-$150 | New patient specials |

facts.fact: The page's channel table lists a monthly budget of $50-$800 for CTV / streaming TV, as a planning band rather than an Adwave quote.
facts.quote: | CTV / Streaming TV | $50-$800 | 4-8 weeks | Varies (brand lift) | Trust and credibility |

facts.fact: The page's channel table lists a monthly budget of $0-$2,500 for local SEO and reviews.
facts.quote: | Local SEO / Reviews | $0-$2,500 | 3-6 months | Low (organic) | Long-term visibility |

facts.fact: The page's channel table lists a monthly budget of $500-$2,500 for direct mail, with a patient acquisition cost of $75-$200.
facts.quote: | Direct Mail | $500-$2,500 | 2-4 weeks | $75-$200 | New movers |

facts.fact: The page cites a WordStream dental cost-per-click figure of $6.69, which it describes as a third-party benchmark rather than a rate card.
facts.quote: WordStream dental CPC $6.69.

facts.fact: The page cites BrightLocal's finding that 87% of consumers read online reviews for local businesses.
facts.quote: BrightLocal: 87% of consumers read online reviews for local businesses.

facts.fact: The page gives a planning convention of 5% to 8% of revenue for established dental practice advertising budgets, and notes this is not a cited ADA dataset.
facts.quote: 5% to 8% of revenue for an established practice.

facts.fact: The page gives a planning convention of 10% to 15% of revenue for new dental practices in their first two years.
facts.quote: 10% to 15% for a new practice.

facts.fact: Adwave's product floor is $30 a day, about $900 a month, for Meta, Google, TikTok, Reddit, web, and TV.
facts.quote: Adwave $30 a day. About $900 a month.

facts.fact: The page recommends $1,500 to $2,500 per month for Google advertising for a new dental practice.
facts.quote: Set aside $1,500 to $2,500/month for Google

facts.fact: For a dental practice collecting $75,000 per month, the page gives a total advertising range of $3,750 to $6,000 per month across all channels, using the 5% to 8% convention.
facts.quote: For a practice collecting $75,000/month, that's $3,750 to $6,000/month across all channels.

facts.fact: The page states that treatment-quoted patients for implants, veneers, or Invisalign often need 2 to 3 touches before committing.
facts.quote: often need 2 to 3 touches before committing.

facts.fact: The page recommends sending a Google review request within 2 hours of a patient's visit.
facts.quote: within 2 hours of their visit.

facts.fact: The page claims review management platforms can increase monthly review volume 5x to 10x, as a vendor-side claim without a cited source.
facts.quote: can increase your monthly review volume 5x to 10x.

facts.fact: The page states that a $200 monthly budget is below a full month at Adwave's $30-per-day floor.
facts.quote: A $200 month is below a full month at that floor.

facts.fact: The page states that claiming a Yelp profile for a dental practice is free.
facts.quote: Claim your free profile and keep it updated, but be cautious with Yelp's paid advertising.

facts.fact: The page states that results from Yelp's paid advertising vary widely by market, and that in some cities Google and Healthgrades dominate dentist discovery instead of Yelp.
facts.quote: Results vary widely by market. In some cities, Yelp is a significant discovery platform for dentists; in others, Google and Healthgrades dominate.
